meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes, indeed', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything, all; that's it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'сказать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'tell', paired with 'рассказывать'.

examples.text: Он же слабый, сразу всё расскажет!
examples.trans: He's weak, after all—he'll tell us everything straight away!

examples.text: Я сегодня же расскажу всё Самсону!
examples.trans: I'll tell Samson everything this very day!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'your', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?
Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'well; come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'стать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to stop, cease', paired with 'переставать'.

examples.text: Иначе я перестану давать тебе деньги!
examples.trans: Otherwise I'll stop giving you money!

examples.text: Приезжай сейчас! Иначе я перестану давать тебе деньги!
examples.trans: Come over right now! Otherwise I'll stop giving you money!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'they', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Настроение у меня действительно очень хорошее.
examples.trans: My mood really is very good.
This is indeed an important question.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for; behind', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
And does the governor support you?

examples.text: Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

переживать.gloss: to worry, to fret; to go through

meanings.en: to worry, to fret; to go through
meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'живать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to worry, to fret; to go through', paired with 'пережить'.

examples.trans: Why are you worrying like that?
Don't worry, everything will be fine.

examples.text: Что вы так переживаете? Самсонов всё, он себя закопал.
examples.trans: Why are you worrying like that? Samsonov is finished, he buried himself.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'nine', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Open the door. Is this flat nine?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'exit; way out' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Как говорит наш губернатор, выход всегда есть.
examples.trans: As our governor says, there's always a way out.

вообще-то.gloss: actually, as a matter of fact

meanings.en: actually, as a matter of fact
meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'обще-то'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Меня вообще-то Юля зовут. Вот сахар.
examples.trans: My name is actually Yulia. Here's the sugar.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'говорить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to have a talk', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.text: Поговори с Аракеляном. Пусть он заберёт заявление.
examples.trans: Talk to Arakelyan. Get him to withdraw his statement.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come, to arrive', paired with 'приходить'.

examples.trans: Security will be here any moment.

examples.text: Не надо, Самсон. Сейчас придёт охрана.
examples.trans: Don't, Samson. Security will be here any second.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'here is; (emphasis) that's', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'after', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Он за мной после концерта ухаживал.
examples.trans: He courted me after a concert once.

examples.text: Он за мной после концерта ухаживал. В Москву звал замуж!
examples.trans: He courted me after a concert once. He asked me to marry him and come to Moscow!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how; as', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'matter; thing to do' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I have a lot to do.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, that; it is', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Как интересно! А в Москве ты про меня гадости рассказываешь.
examples.trans: How interesting! And in Moscow you go around saying nasty things about me.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'except', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ни у кого в городе нет денег, кроме Игнатьева.
examples.trans: Nobody in town has any money, except Ignatyev.
I am speaking seriously, no joking!

examples.text: Воспитательница кричит на всех, кроме Петухова!
examples.trans: The teacher yells at everyone except Petukhov!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'someone, somebody', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Finally someone is for the people!

examples.text: Слушай, тут пишут: «Гордость России! Наконец-то кто-то за народ!»
examples.trans: Listen, here they write: 'Pride of Russia! Finally someone is for the people!'

examples.text: Ты что, не понимаешь? Я задавить кого-то мог!
examples.trans: Don't you understand? I could have run someone over!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to prowl, wander around'.

examples.text: Интересно, кроме меня здесь кто-то шастал?
examples.trans: I wonder if anyone else has been snooping around here besides me?

examples.text: На кухне никто не хочет шастать без причины.
examples.trans: In the kitchen nobody wants to prowl without a reason.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'such, like this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ексуальный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('sexy, attractive').

examples.trans: You are so sexy when you get jealous.

examples.text: Ты тоже такая сексуальная, когда я ревную.
examples.trans: You are so sexy too when I get jealous.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'when', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: When I grow up, I'll be the mayor.

examples.text: Когда вырасту, ты будешь просить у меня прощения!
examples.trans: When I grow up, you'll be begging me to forgive you!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be jealous of'.

related.gloss: to be jealous for a while

examples.trans: Are you jealous of my past?
Max, tell the truth, are you jealous?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'too, also', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы же здесь выросли. И о людях тоже надо думать.
examples.trans: After all, we grew up here. And you have to think about people too.
